items.title: Default: ecology cadence 1,500 -> 3,000 ticks
items.detail: Ruled YES (R37). v7.1 defaults ecology.cadence to 3,000 and migrates saved configs once. Before: The sweep found no effect of the ecology pass cadence on a wolf pack against herds 45-60 tiles away, in both cell orders. A 3,000-tick default halves the passes and their fuse time at no measured cost. Not applied to v7.0 (cfg.ecology.cadence is still 1500).
items.evidence: SW1+SW1R, 4 reps: wolf attacks on placed herds ctl 174, cad500 243, cad6000 145; placed prey killed 1/2/0
items.next: Test at the testing stage: region8 forts, n = 5 reps per arm, fresh load per arm, counterbalanced, every animal wiped first.

items.title: Default: ecology nudge off
items.detail: Ruled YES (R38). v7.1 defaults the nudge off; `groups nudge` still turns it on, and 'all on' no longer does. Before: Neither the current nudge (40 tiles / 3,000 t / r6) nor a tighter one changed kills or attacks against off, once cell order was controlled. RELS shows DF brings the fight itself once a relation exists, and off means no visible teleports. Not applied (ecology.nudge=true).
items.evidence: SW1+SW1R pooled: nudge_off 179 attacks / 3 placed kills vs ctl 174 / 1; nudge_tight 198 / 1
items.next: Test at the testing stage: region8 forts, n = 5 reps per arm, fresh load per arm, counterbalanced, every animal wiped first.

items.title: Default: pack_sneak 0 and retire the SNEAK write (rejected; SNEAK kept)
items.detail: Rejected (R8, R40, R58; Part 1 ruling on item 12): SNEAK stays. SW2 never wrote SNEAK (the placed pack was never a tracked group, so no pairing reached the 0.25 share), so its null was vacuous. v7.1 keeps pack_sneak 0.25 and writes skill profiles 0-20 (solitary apex 15, pack baseline 5, pack bonus 10) to the caste NATURAL_SKILL and the unit, with a readback. Before: Sneak bonus 0 / 0.25 / 1.0 made no measurable difference in either cell order, matching STL/STL2 (wild AI never hides). Setting pack_sneak 0 removes one class of unit writes; the 0.05 pack-mass floor stays because the arena cannot isolate it from DF's own aiming of placed units.
items.evidence: SW2+SW2R placed prey killed over 4 reps: ctl 4, sneak0 4, sneak100 0; STL/STL2 hidden 0 of 426 samples
items.next: Post-alpha: SNK-L (SNEAK 0/5/10/15/20 on the caste before placement, forced hidden start) and SNK1-2. Test at the testing stage: region8 forts, n = 5 reps per arm, fresh load per arm, counterbalanced, every animal wiped first.

items.title: Remove the builder's x3 pack-hunter pick bonus (rejected; bonus kept and fixed)
items.detail: Ruled KEEP (R41): the lack of effect was probably a handling failure. v7.1 fixed three defects: it read a floored cluster midpoint (a 1:2 hunter counted as solitary), the seed was always the alphabetically first linkable species, and animal people carried their root's cluster. Before: SW7 rosters built with bonus 1, 3 and 5 gave the same land groups and fights on CTRL; design rule R11 already treats the x3 as a contrived weight. The rig test was weak (only 7-8 of 27-29 wanted species exist in CTRL's pool), while the desk D1 shows rosters change at every level (pack-hunt presence 57% -> 77%).
items.evidence: SW7: land groups 3.1/1.6 (x1), 2.2/2.2 (x3), 3.3/2.8 (x5), attacks 0 in all cells; D1: 100% of CTRL keys change
items.next: Test at the testing stage: region8 forts, n = 5 reps per arm, fresh load per arm, counterbalanced, every animal wiped first.

items.title: Drop the apex step from the FREQUENCY ladder; steer apexes by placement and stock
items.detail: Ruled YES (R34), with the pyramid targets as the first default (R9: apex on land present 20-30% of the season). v7.1 takes the apex step off the ladder, caps an apex's raw FREQUENCY at 5, and places apex groups from stock toward the presence target (1 group on calm maps, 2 on savage). Before: The apex FREQUENCY does not visibly bring apexes: 0 apex arrivals in all 4 CTRL season runs, 0-3 elsewhere, and apex present in 1 of 6 SW4 runs at any predator multiplier. Steering apexes then needs a mechanism the tool lacks today: a placed or stocked apex group (one LP group per map, two on savage maps, design R12.7).
items.evidence: S8C/S8Cb CTRL apex 0,0,0,0; S8B 0,3 cheetah; S8O 2,1 anaconda; SW4 apex present 1 of 6
items.next: FQ1 (FREQUENCY 1-100 incrementally) and APX tests at the testing stage; n = 5, region8.

items.title: Cavern groups-at-once: a fixed 5 per layer under the tool's control
items.detail: Superseded by R44: the tool gates every cavern layer at a fixed 5 concurrent groups, natives counted; it releases under the cap, holds at FREQUENCY 1 at the cap and trims over it. The magma/underworld layer is never touched (R60). Before: Caps of 1 and 2 cut the tool's own cavern groups by about 40% but never approach the cap, because DF's native cavern populations (4-5 groups per depth) are not the tool's to gate. The Layers tab presents it as a ceiling, which misleads.
items.evidence: SW5: cavern groups 24.0/27.3 at auto vs 13.7-16.0 at caps 1 and 2, same in both orders
items.next: Test at the testing stage: region8 forts, n = 5 reps per arm, fresh load per arm, counterbalanced, every animal wiped first.

items.title: Optional: water groups-at-once default 2 per body
items.detail: Ruled NO (R45): no '2 per body' default. v7.1 manages each water body like land (the map-size or fixed cap) with no hard ceiling, retries failed draws, and reads land-layer ocean entries, aiming for 3-5 concurrent aquatic groups on a fort map. Before: On BOATS the water supply is only 2-5 groups, so cap 2 matched auto and the cap rarely binds; a default of 2 would mean less placement. Evidence is thin: one map, and cap 1 held exactly only in one replicate.
items.evidence: SW6: water groups auto 4.8/2.1, w2 3.1/2.3, w1 1.0/2.1
items.next: G2 per layer, including water bodies. Test at the testing stage: region8 forts, n = 5 reps per arm, fresh load per arm, counterbalanced, every animal wiped first.

items.title: Should carnivorous swimmers count as scavengers?
items.detail: Ruled YES (R42), sharks included (R17). v7.1's MODEL.swimScavenger counts carnivorous swimmers (sharks, crocodiles, alligators, orcas; not whale sharks); they reach remains through water hops and a 2-tile wet reach. Before: SCAV.is counts a scavenger only if it is BONECARN, a CURIOUS_BEAST_EATER or on SCAV.TEXT; among vanilla swimmers that leaves only POND_GRABBER, SEA_SERPENT and SEA_MONSTER, so alligators, crocodiles and sharks never scavenge and scav_ext's swimmer path has almost no vanilla users. Water carcasses were cleared in SCV2Wb with pond grabbers or wolves on the bank.
items.evidence: SCV2Wb: 6 -> 0 carp carcasses in all 4 cells; SCVW: alligators walked 0 of 5
items.next: SCV3 water arms. Test at the testing stage: region8 forts, n = 5 reps per arm, fresh load per arm, counterbalanced, every animal wiped first.

items.title: Group-size cap for animal people (plump helmet men) in caverns
items.detail: Ruled YES (R35): animal-person group size in the caverns is capped (default 5) and the cap lifts while that cavern irrupts. Before: With the builder on, plump helmet men filled the cavern shore-prey slot and arrived about 15 per wave, 54 and 180 units in a season on BOATS (33 died in rep 1). The ladder sets wave share, not unit share, so a large-cluster species swamps the layer. A cap via cfg.group_size (the mechanism v7 outgun_cap already writes) is the obvious lever.
items.evidence: S8B BOATS: PLUMP_HELMET_MAN 54 and 180 units, 7 and 12 waves
items.next: Test at the testing stage: region8 forts, n = 5 reps per arm, fresh load per arm, counterbalanced, every animal wiped first.

items.title: Add invasive must place SAVAGE species on calm maps itself

items.title: Builder port: marked Done, but v7.0 writes the v2.1 ladder and omits v2.2 pieces
items.detail: Ruled: port approved (R57). v7.1 ports ladder22 inside each trophic level with the pyramid targets for level totals, a biomass guard, the flying layer, SN/SNP slots, the GIANT_* boost and the GOBBLE edge table; weights target units (R59). Before: Tracker 5 says the port is Done (0d030b2) while recommendation 14 says 'its port into v7.0 is next'. The code confirms a partial port: ROSTER.LADDER uses v2.1 base values (land AL 3, ML 3, GZ 6) rather than ladder22 (AL 4, ML 2, GZ 10.5), which the desk predicts gives about 31% land predators instead of 16%, yet S8 was read against the v2.2 14-18% target. The port also collapses ocean/lake/river and cav1-3 into three layers, has no flying apex or SNP slot, and boosts giants by mass only. Also absent (1 Oct review, ROSTER.SLOTS at seasonal-wildlife.lua v7.0 ~5070): a flying layer (RP and LB sit in the land table), the SNP slot, the GOBBLE_VERMIN edge table and vermin stock links. design.md section 9 lists them.

items.title: Why OCEAN2's optional pelagic slot came out empty
items.detail: Answered (Part 1 C s8, v7.1 roster): ocean life rides land-layer entries, which v7.0's water roster never read, and the survey stopped at the top level. Ruled (R14, R59): a shallow ocean seats a pelagic slot. v7.1 seats APE and PE slots on any ocean map and lets prey pull pelagic predators in. Before: The report first said the pelagic slot 'stays closed' on shallow maps; the code keeps it optional (min 0, max 1) on any ocean and raises it to 2 with triple weight only where deep columns exist. The report is corrected. Still open: on OCEAN2 the slot was left empty in both builds. No pelagic candidate in OCEAN2's pool, or the builder's min 0 skipping it, would both explain it.

items.title: Should the ladder target units rather than waves?
items.detail: Ruled (R59): the ladder targets units (FREQUENCY divided by mean cluster size). Built in v7.1. Before: FREQUENCY sets each species' share of waves, but the overshoot on BOATS came from pack size: giant jackal packs made 27 units with modest wave counts, putting predators at 42% of surface units in one replicate. Dividing a group species' FREQUENCY by its mean cluster size would target unit share; the same issue drives the plump-helmet-man swamp.
items.evidence: S8B rep 1: GIANT_JACKAL 27 units, predators 47% of waves / 42% of units

items.title: Demons arriving on CTRL's deep layer are left unmanaged (D8)
items.detail: Ruled (R60): demons on the deep layers have no limit and no management, unseen until breached; the tool has no impact on them. v7.1 never keys, counts, holds or writes the magma/underworld layer. Before: The jobs average about 1% of wall time; what players feel are spikes (groups 67-149 ms, ecology 58-71 ms) and jobs landing on shared ticks, plus the overlay decoding JSON and scanning pairs every render frame, and the undo ring re-encoded per edit. Lua runs on DF's one simulation thread, so the levers are avoided work, native scans and staggering, not threads. Proposals P0-P7 of the analysis.
